chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, raising it, said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever the meal was placed in front of him, said: 'Glory be to You, O Allah! How Goodly You are Testing us. Glory be to You! How frequently You are Feeding us. Glory be to You! How frequently You are Excusing us. O Allah! Expand upon us and upon the poor Believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women'.

key_terms.الْمَائِدَةُ: The meal or food placed for eating
key_terms.سُبْحَانَكَ: Glory be to You (an expression of praising God's perfection)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited by the Prophet (SAWW) before eating?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on recognizing divine blessings through both sustenance ('what You give us') and trials ('what You test us with'), reflecting a holistic view of gratitude. The Prophet’s invocation extends personal thanksgiving to include the broader community of believers, underscoring the social dimension of worship in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, raising it, said,

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever the meal was placed in front of him<sup>saww</sup>, said: ‘Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup>! O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! How Goodly You<sup>azwj</sup> are Testing us. How frequently You<sup>azwj</sup> are Feeding us Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup>! How frequently You<sup>azwj</sup> are Excusing us. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Expand upon us and upon the poor Believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy in a marfu’ manner has said, the following: “The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,

when food was made available for him said, ‘O Lord, You are free of all defects, how good is Your trial for us. O Lord, You are free of all defects, and how great is what You have granted us, O Lord, You are free of all defects, how often it is that You give us good health, O Lord, expand our sustenance and for the poor believers, male and female and Muslims.’”
